questions.q: A goose issue sits in Inbox and a contributor wants to implement it. Per AGENTS.md, the correct action is:
options: Help resolve the issue discussion; only Status Ready issues may be implemented
Implement immediately since speed helps triage
Ask GitHub support to move it to Ready
Only implement it if the title contains the word 'fix'
explanation: Implementing Inbox issues is explicitly prohibited; triage first, code later.
Support moves no board statuses; maintainers do.
Title keywords are not a triage criterion.

questions.q: Which template structure does .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug_report.md demand?
options: Description, To Reproduce steps, Expected behavior, plus diagnostics zip guidance
Only a one-line summary typed in the title
An attached gdb backtrace for every bug
A link to a pre-opened PR as proof
explanation: The template requires body sections, not just a title.
Backtraces are not required by the template; the diagnostics zip is.
Bugs and PRs are filed separately; no proof link is required.

questions.q: In the real v1.49.0 history, `509fcac69` is:
options: fix(token_counter): fix panic with GitHub Copilot (#4632)
the commit that introduced the state machine
the version bump to 1.49.0
the desktop UI freeze fix
explanation: The state machine evolved over many commits; no single introduction hash is this one.
The 1.49.0 bump is dd8de0196.
The desktop freeze fix is ec96aa059.

questions.q: The most useful form of a bug reproduction for a maintainer is:
options: A minimal runnable script whose exit code distinguishes good from bad behavior
A video of the bug happening once
A 200-line stack trace with no input data
A theory of which commit caused it, without verification
explanation: Videos cannot be re-executed or asserted against.
A trace without inputs is not rerunnable.
Theories without a runnable check are not reproductions.

questions.q: git bisect's exit-code contract under `git bisect run`:
options: 0 = good, 1-127 excluding 125 = bad, 125 = skip
0 = bad, 1 = good — inverted from manual bisect
Any exit code ends the bisect and marks the commit bad
Exit codes are ignored; output text decides
explanation: The run convention matches manual semantics: 0 good, non-zero bad (125 skip).
Only exhaustive manual resets behave that way; run stops when a first bad commit is found.
Output text is never parsed by bisect run.

questions.q: On a 6-commit history with one regression, why is bisect exponentially better than cherry-pick hunting?
options: Each repro run halves the remaining candidate space (~log2 N runs)
Bisect runs the test suite in parallel on all commits
Bisect reads the commit messages to guess the bug
Bisect uses the reflog to skip commits automatically
explanation: Bisect checks out one commit at a time; there is no parallel execution.
Messages are not parsed for bug-guessing; the repro is the judge.
The reflog is unrelated to bisect's midpoint search.

questions.q: With no RUST_LOG set, goose's EnvFilter (logging.rs:30-38) defaults to:
options: goose=info and mcp_client=info, WARN for the rest
trace for the entire workspace
error only
RUST_LOG=off semantics with no output
explanation: Whole-workspace trace is never the default.
INFO/WARN baseline beats error-only.
Output is not off; the defaults are deliberately conservative but active.

questions.q: The `--test-threads=1` run fixes a test that fails only in CI most reliably when the test's real problem is:
options: Shared global state mutated by multiple tests
Compilation timeouts
Missing dev-dependencies
Unstable network requests to the crates.io API at test time
explanation: Thread count does not affect compile time.
Missing dev-deps fail deterministically regardless of threads.
crates.io is not queried during test execution.

questions.q: Which of these is the repo's expected use of .snap files?
options: Accept deliberate diffs through the documented insta update path, and review .snap changes in the PR
Hand-edit .snap text when the prompt changes
Delete .snap files whenever a test fails to regenerate clean
Keep .snap files in .gitignore to avoid noise
explanation: Hand-editing fights the tool that owns the files.
Deleting evidence to pass is exactly the anti-pattern.
.snap files are tracked (only .snap.new is gitignored) because they are evidence.

questions.q: Doctrine: a mock provider in goose tests such as mcp_integration_test.rs:44 is defined how?
options: As a plain struct implementing the real Provider trait inside the test crate
By subclassing the base provider class with mock overrides
By recording HTTP traffic with mitmproxy at test setup
By pointing the provider at a localhost echo server
explanation: There is no class hierarchy; the trait is the seam.
Traffic proxies are not how the crate builds its in-process mock.
An echo server would be an MCP fixture concern, not a provider mock.

questions.q: What does record mode write and replay mode read in the MCP integration test?
options: Responses keyed to request inputs under crates/goose/tests/mcp_replays/
Only the timestamps of each tool call
Screenshots of the running server console
A truncated log of the last server restart
explanation: Timestamps alone are insufficient to replay responses.
Console screenshots are not replayable data.
Restart logs carry no response payloads.

questions.q: In Justfile:456-458, after the record run the recipe runs `git add crates/goose/tests/mcp_replays/` because:
options: Replays are committed evidence — the recorded artifacts must be staged for review with the change
Git requires test fixtures to be staged before cargo test
The directory might otherwise be deleted by cargo clean
CI only runs tests whose fixtures are listed in the index
explanation: cargo test does not require staged fixtures.
cargo clean removes build artifacts, not src/tests directories.
CI decides test selection, not the git index.

questions.q: The root Cargo.toml sets `string_slice = "warn"` at [workspace.lints.clippy]. The fix pattern for that lint is:
options: get(..) with an explicit fallback/error decision instead of direct slicing
Always disable the lint at crate level
Convert all strings to ASCII-Latin-1 before slicing
Slice only inside unsafe blocks
explanation: Crate-level allows hide the risk the lint exists for.
Encoding conversion changes the data; slicing correctness remains the issue.
unsafe slicing still panics at boundaries — no help.

questions.q: In the v1.49.0 checkout, deny.toml's advisory policy sets `unmaintained = "none"` and `unsound = "none"` while `yanked = "deny"`. The design intent is:
options: Mirror cargo-audit semantics: hard-block yanked crates, stay silent on the more opinionated categories unless a reason is documented
Yanked and unmaintained crates are both irrelevant to CI
Only crates with active CVEs are ever blocked
All three categories were disabled to speed up CI runs
explanation: The comment in the file states it emulates cargo-audit: vulns+yanked checked, unmaintained/unsound not.
CVE blocking is one part; yanked is an independent hard failure beyond CVEs.
Levels are a security-policy choice, not a performance knob.

questions.q: A contributor fixes a tool-label truncation in crates/goose/src/agents/agent.rs only. Per AGENTS.md:32 a maintainer must flag:
options: Missing parity — the same behavior in the state-machine path needs the fix and a test too
The file choice — agent.rs is not the right location for labels
The change being too small to review
Missing a benchmark table in the PR body
explanation: agent.rs is a legitimate location; the objection is incompleteness across universes.
Small focused fixes are welcome in this repo.
Benchmarks are not a review requirement for correctness fixes.

questions.q: state_machine::enabled() returns true for which env value?
options: GOOSE_STATE_MACHINE=TRUE
GOOSE_STATE_MACHINE=2
GOOSE_STATE_MACHINE=false
GOOSE_STATE_MACHINE=
explanation: Only the spellings 1/true/TRUE/yes enable the path; 2 is not one of them.
false is not in the accepted set and falls back to legacy.
An empty value also falls through to legacy (unwrap_or(false)).

questions.q: A correct parity regression test for an agent-loop fix must:
options: Run the SAME assertion pinned once to GOOSE_STATE_MACHINE=0 and once to =1 via scoped env guards
Run once with the env var unset to cover both paths
Randomize the env var per CI job
Test only the state-machine path since legacy is deprecated
explanation: Unset picks the legacy default — the second path never runs.
Randomization makes failures unreproducible.
Legacy is live until migration completes; ignoring it ships buggy behavior to current users.

questions.q: Where do the repo's own parity tests pin the env var, showing the approved pattern?
options: agent_reply.rs and agent.rs tests using env_lock::lock_env / clear_otel_env guards
In build.rs at compile time
In docker-compose environment blocks
Inside the Provider trait impls
explanation: build.rs runs before tests and cannot pin per-test runtime state.
No compose-based pinning exists for Rust test env.
Provider impls are test-agnostic production code.

questions.q: The correct full sequence a feature PR must document, per AGENTS.md:94:
options: impl → tests → goose-self-test.yaml scenario added → rebuild → goose run --recipe goose-self-test.yaml
recipe scenario first, code after validation, tests optional
unit tests only; recipes are optional for small features
impl → cargo publish → update recipe if time permits
explanation: The recipe validates the code, so it comes after the impl lands.
The rule does not exempt small features from the recipe update.
cargo publish is release work, never a feature-validation step.

questions.q: The feature_request template ordering — problem, outcome, approaches — exists to make the issue:
options: Judged on the outcome before any implementation is preselected
Long enough to satisfy GitHub search indexing
Compatible with the Issues board kanban columns
Auto-generatable from PR descriptions
explanation: Search indexing is not a template design goal.
Board compatibility is about status fields, not body order.
Templates shape issues, not PR description generation.

questions.q: The `{{ test_phases }}` placeholder inside goose-self-test.yaml's prompt is filled from:
options: The parameters block, overridable by CLI key-value flags at run time
The environment variable TEST_PHASES only
The recipe's title block
Hard-coded session state JSON
explanation: Env vars are not the recipe's parameter channel.
The title is static display text.
No session-state JSON powers recipe interpolation.

questions.q: A recipe run blocked by a missing provider configuration should be handled in a PR verification plan by:
options: Stating the exact blocker and the planned command, then validating once a provider is available
Claiming the run passed with an invented summary
Skipping the recipe update entirely
Running only cargo test and calling it equivalent
explanation: Fabricated run results are the one unrecoverable failure mode.
The rule requires the recipe update regardless of local run ability.
Unit tests and recipe runs validate different layers; they are not equivalent.

questions.q: A tool response above the large_response_handler threshold results in:
options: A spill to a temp file and a pointer message, keeping the transcript small
A silent truncation to the threshold in-place
A rejected tool call with a user-facing error
The full text re-encoded to tokens to save space
explanation: Truncation loses data; the handler preserves it on disk.
The result is relocated, not rejected.
Re-encoding does not reduce content; tokenization is not compression.

questions.q: Why is the token counter cache bounded at 1,024 entries with a hash-keyed LRU?
options: Duplicate content (repeated prompts, tool schemas) avoids expensive tokenization, while memory stays constant
Rust requires all LRU caches to be exactly 1,024 entries
The tokenizer can only produce 1,024 distinct outputs per session
CI enforces a 1,024-crate limit in the dependency graph
explanation: The bound is a design constant (MAX_TOKEN_CACHE_SIZE), not a language limit.
Tokenizer output space is unbounded; only the cache is bounded.
Dependency limits are unrelated to in-memory caching.

questions.q: Reviewing a diff that adds a new dependency, the two consistency checks besides advisories are:
options: Dependency added via cargo add and Cargo.lock updated consistently
Dependency pinned to exactly three minor versions and vendored under vendor/
Dependency has more than 1,000 GitHub stars and a sponsor page
Dependency is compiled with --release in CI before merge
explanation: Triple version pinning and vendoring are not repo requirements.
Stars and sponsorship are popularity signals, not policy.
Release-mode prebuilding is not a merge gate for dependencies.

miniLab.title: Real PR simulator: land a UTF-8-safe bug fix on your fork (scratch)
miniLab.instructions:
Simulate the full Unit 2 pipeline in a LOCAL scratch repo (not the real goose repository).

1. Create `u2-exam-fork/` under your labs directory. `git init` it and scaffold a tiny Rust lib crate inside with `cargo new --lib u2-exam-fork/fixer`.
2. Seed the bug in `fixer/src/lib.rs`: a `pub fn truncate_label(text: &str, max: usize) -> String` that does `text[..max]` byte slicing — it panics on multibyte text and corrupts labels.
3. Implement the fix: char-boundary-safe truncation (e.g. `text.chars().take(max).collect()` with an exact-fit fast path). Do not add comments that restate code.
4. Add two regression tests in `fixer/tests/truncate_label_regression.rs`: (a) `multibyte_label_never_panics` — multibyte input longer than max returns valid UTF-8 with exactly `max` chars; (b) `exact_fit_returns_original` — input of exactly `max` chars is returned unchanged.
5. Write `fixer/PR.md` with: the issue link line (dummy Ready issue URL is fine), one-paragraph implementation note, a `## Tests` section listing both regression test names, and a verification plan section that MUST contain these lines: `fmt: cargo fmt --check`, `clippy: cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, `parity: checked both legacy and state-machine paths (agent-loop drill from l06/l08)`, `state machine: GOOSE_STATE_MACHINE=1 run (mock provider drill)`.
6. Run `cargo fmt`, `cargo test`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` in `fixer/` so the checks below pass.

This simulates, in lightweight form, the real auto-grade: fmt + clippy + tests + parity note + GOOSE_STATE_MACHINE=1 run — on a scratch crate instead of the goose workspace.
